newsitem.title: LATVIA: COMMISSION SEES COMPETITIVE PRESSURES IN EU.
newsitem.headline: COMMISSION SEES COMPETITIVE PRESSURES IN EU.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday said that Latvia would face serious problems coping with competition in the European Union but has made progress to forming a market economy.
In its conclusions on Latvia, the Commission said that the country was a democracy but needed, like Estonia, to accelerate the naturalisation of its large Russian population.
Of the Baltic states, the Commission recommended beginning talks only with Estonia in a first wave of enlargement.

"Latvia has made considerable progress in the creation of a market economy but it would face serious difficulties to cope with competitive pressure and market forces within the Union in the medium term," the Commission said.
It said that trade and prices had largely been liberalised and that headway had been made in stabilising the economy.
"While there has been significant progress in establishing the legislative framework, effective implementation is lagging behind," it added.
It said all the necessary legislative bodies were not in place.
"Privatisation is not complete; the remaining state-owned companies are generally in poor financial condition and there is a shortage of investors," it said.
It also said that the economy was relatively open with low labour costs but that exports consisted mainly of low value-added goods.
"Industrial restructuring as well as enterprise restructuring is still needed. The banking sector is underdeveloped and weak in parts," it added.
